title: Turn a Callable into a lazy Supplier

blocks.text: `Supplier.get()` cannot throw a checked exception, while `Callable.call()` declares `throws Exception`. Both take no arguments and return a value, so the bridge from one to the other is a small wrapper.
Write `Tasks.unchecked(Callable<T> task)`. It returns a `Supplier<T>` whose `get()` calls the task and returns its result. Failures leave `get()` like this:
A `Supplier` is lazy: think about when the task should run, and how often.

cases.says: get() returns what the task returns.
Nothing runs when the Supplier is built; each get() runs the task again.
An IOException leaves as an UncheckedIOException carrying the original as its cause.
Any other checked exception leaves as a RuntimeException carrying the original as its cause.
An exception that is already unchecked is rethrown as it is.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: get() cannot throw a checked exception, so a checked failure is wrapped in an unchecked one.
